name: Ganesha - painted temple figurine
prompt: Create one exquisite, respectful South Indian Ganesha miniature figurine pendant for a small desktop charm, a believable hand-painted temple keepsake with fine material detail and warm natural studio light. Ganesha is seated, recognizable elephant head with a single gently curved trunk, calm kind eyes, full body including feet and four clearly separated arms. Warm natural terracotta skin, rich crimson and saffron silk dhoti with gold edging, tasteful gold crown and jewelry; one hand blessing, one with a small modak bowl. IMPORTANT: show three distinct horizontal white sacred-ash vibhuti stripes (pattai / tripundra) across the broad forehead, with a small central red kumkum dot. The stripes must be crisp and recognizable, not one vertical tilak. Use realistic painted resin/bronze craftsmanship rather than a cartoon, chibi, toy emoji, anime or shiny plastic. A small closed gold hanging eyelet sits centered above the crown, fully inside the canvas; NO chain or cord. The entire figure is visible and centered, including the base and eyelet. Keep the silhouette bold and readable at 72 by 84 pixels, with a sufficiently prominent face for the forehead detail. Portrait subject within a square 1024px image; leave a clean 10 percent empty margin on every side. Isolate on perfectly flat bright chroma green #00FF00; no ground, shadows on the background, scenery, lettering, watermarks, borders or extra objects. The green is only a removable background: no green clothing or green reflection on the subject. Beautiful, dignified, recognizable South Indian religious artistry.
